summary: Jinchuan Wan is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who held professorships at National Central University and Fo Guang University, both attested in 2010.

Jing Yin is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under K. L. Dhammajoti (attested 1995). They served as Director at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2006–2010) and taught several students, including Rangama Chandawimala and Yu Yan Pang.

Jing-shen Tao is a historian and sinologist who studied at National Taiwan University (~1952–1959) and Indiana University Bloomington (~1963–1967, Ph.D.). He served as Professor of East Asian Studies at the University of Arizona (~1976–2000).
Jingru Wang was a scholar in linguistics and history/archaeology. He studied at Tsinghua University (~1926–1930) and held a post at Minzu University of China from ~1952 to 1990.
Jingyi Yang works in Indology, Tibetology, and computational studies. In 2026, she is attested as a student and Wissenschaftliche Projektmitarbeiterin at the University of Hamburg.

Jinhua Chen specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. He pursued graduate studies at McMaster University, conducted postdoctoral research at Kyoto University under Noritoshi Aramaki, and served as professor of East Asian Buddhism at the University of British Columbia (attested 2008–2018).

Jinhua Jia is a scholar of sinology, religious studies, and philosophy who earned her PhD at the University of Colorado Boulder under Paul W. Kroll (1994–1999). Her career includes posts at Harvard, Hong Kong Polytechnic University, and the University of Macau.
Jinling He is a scholar in Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Hiroki Okumura.
Jinping Liao is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin.
Jinshi Fan is a scholar of archaeology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Su Bai at Peking University (~1958–1963) and served as Director of the Dunhuang Academy from 1984 to 2014.

Jinzhang Peng was a scholar in archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He served at Wuhan University (~1963–1986) before joining the Dunhuang Academy, where he was dean of the archeological institute (~1986–2005) and a researcher/professor (~1986–2017).
Jiro Abe was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1903–1907). He held posts at Japan Women's University (~1913–1923) and Tohoku University (~1923–1945).

Jiro Kawakita was a scholar in Tibetology and other fields. After studying at Kyoto University (~1939–1943), he held posts at Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1960–1977), the University of Tsukuba (~1977–1985), and Chubu University (~1985–1992).
Jiro Murata was a scholar of history, archaeology, and sinology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1916–1920) and held a post at the National Institute of Technology, Akashi College (~1962–1967).

Jiro Sugiyama was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1948–1953). He held posts at the Tokyo National Museum (~1953–1988) and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (~1996–2004).
Jiryo Masuda was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Unrai Wogihara. He served as a Professor at the University of Calcutta, where he taught Prabodh Chandra Bagchi.
Jishu Oda was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as Rector at Choboji Monastery (attested 1914) and later as Professor Emeritus at Shuchiin University (attested 1977).

Jitendra Nath Banerjea was a scholar in history, archaeology, Indology, and religious studies. He studied under Hemchandra Raychaudhuri (~1916–1918) and served as Carmichael Professor of Ancient Indian History and Culture at the University of Calcutta (~1918–1959).

Jitendra Nath Mohanty was a philosopher and Indologist who studied at Calcutta, Presidency, and Göttingen (Ph.D. ~1952–1954). He taught at the University of Oklahoma (~1972–1986) and Temple University (~1986–2007), and founded the journal Husserl Studies.
Jitsushyu Oshika is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tohoku University and served as a professor at Toyo University (attested 1980–1981).
